title: A Borel reduction that eventually satisfies push-forward preserves Scott sentence complexity above a threshold
source_title: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of prop:push-forwardssc, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Borel reduction between classes of structures
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Borel reduction Phi from the models of sigma to the models of tau, measurable at some level of the Borel hierarchy, whose image is Borel.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the proposition.

standard_prerequisites.name: Push-forward property
standard_prerequisites.statement: Phi eventually satisfies push-forward when there is a rank delta such that every infinitary formula of rank at least delta over tau has a formula of the same rank over sigma pulling back along Phi.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the second hypothesis and the tool the proof uses.

standard_prerequisites.name: Scott sentence complexity
standard_prerequisites.statement: SSC(A) is the least rank of a Scott sentence for A, and SR(A) is the Scott rank.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity shown to be preserved above a threshold.

core_obligations: Read off the measurability rank lambda of Phi and the rank beta of a formula chi describing its Borel image (source lines 707-709).
For a structure A whose Scott sentence phi has rank epsilon beyond delta, show that phi* together with chi is a Scott sentence for Phi(A) of the same rank (source lines 710-712).
In the other direction use the pull-back theorem to turn a Scott sentence of Phi(A) into one for A whose rank is lambda plus epsilon (source lines 713-715).
Conclude that Scott sentence complexity is preserved once the Scott rank of A exceeds the maximum of lambda times epsilon, delta and beta (source lines 715-717).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix the complexity levels of the reduction and of a description of its image.
Push a Scott sentence forward and add the description of the image.
Pull a Scott sentence back with the pull-back theorem.
Combine the two rank bounds into a threshold.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled proposition at source0.tex lines 696-704: if a Borel reduction Phi between the model classes of two vocabularies has Borel image and eventually satisfies push-forward, then above a threshold on the Scott rank the Scott sentence complexities of A and Phi(A) agree. The statement gives no bound and no construction, while the proof (source lines 706-718) has to manufacture one from three independent pieces of data: the measurability rank lambda of the reduction, the rank beta of a formula describing its image, and the rank delta from which the push-forward property starts to hold. It pushes a Scott sentence of A forward to one for Phi(A) by conjoining the pushed formula with the description of the image, pulls a Scott sentence of Phi(A) back with the pull-back theorem to get one for A of rank lambda plus epsilon, and then reads off the threshold at which the two bounds meet. The interaction of the three ranks is the whole content and it is invisible in the statement.
